title: Campaign, Ad Set, Ad Structure
objectives: Memorize the 3-level structure of every Meta advertising campaign
Identify which settings live at each level

blocks.text: Every single Meta ad in the world follows a strict 3-level hierarchy. Let's master it!

blocks.title: Building a House Analogy
blocks.text: Level 1 (Campaign) is the Blueprint: what kind of house are we building? Level 2 (Ad Set) is the Rooms: who stays in which room, and what is the budget? Level 3 (Ad) is the Furniture & Paint: what does it look like to visitors?

blocks.title: What Lives Where?
items: Level 1: Campaign — Your business goal (e.g., Leads, Sales, Traffic)
Level 2: Ad Set — Audience targeting, locations, placements, schedule & budget
Level 3: Ad — Video, image, headline, text, and Call-to-Action button

blocks.text: One campaign can contain multiple ad sets (e.g., Bengaluru audience vs Delhi audience), and each ad set can hold multiple ads!
Never change your objective after creating a campaign. If your goal changes, create a new campaign.

quiz.q: At which level of the Meta structure do you define your target location (e.g. Pune, 10km radius)?
quiz.hint: Who, where, and when are set at the middle level.
quiz.explain: Ad Set controls the audience demographics, locations, placements, and budgets.

quiz.q: Where do you write your ad headline and upload your product video?
quiz.hint: Think of the creative that the user actually sees.
quiz.explain: The Ad level holds the actual creative assets: images, videos, captions, and links.

quiz.q: True or False: A single campaign can have multiple ad sets targeting different cities.
quiz.hint: One campaign goal can test different audiences.
quiz.explain: True. You can test Ad Set A (Mumbai) and Ad Set B (Delhi) under the same Leads campaign.

quiz.q: Place the 3 structural levels in order from top to bottom.
quiz.explain: Campaign holds Ad Sets, and Ad Sets hold Ads.

recap: Ad Set = Audience, Placements, Budget (Who and Where). Ad = Creative and Copy (What they see).
